text: Pthreads share one {{c1::address space}} and sync with mutexes. MPI runs {{c2::separate processes}} that pass messages. Warp keeps {{c3::host and device}} memory apart, so data gets copied to the GPU first.
extra: This is the memory and communication row of the study guide's comparison table.

text: Pthreads run threads on one {{c1::shared-memory}} machine. MPI runs processes across {{c2::one or more nodes}}. Warp pairs a CPU host with an {{c3::Nvidia GPU}}, or falls back to the CPU.
extra: This is the execution target row of the comparison table.

text: Pthreads give you {{c1::barriers}}, and you write reductions yourself. MPI ships {{c2::collectives}} like Bcast, Reduce, and Allreduce. Warp gives you {{c3::kernel launches}} over \(N\) elements.
extra: Pthreads has no collectives at all. That gap is one reason MPI suits big distributed jobs.

text: Use Pthreads for {{c1::fine-grained}} updates to shared state. Use MPI for {{c2::large independent chunks}} with modest messaging between steps. Use Warp for large {{c3::data-parallel}} maps with uniform work that pays for the copies.
extra: Pick the model by how often the workers need to talk and how big each piece of work is.

text: Pthreads code breaks from {{c1::data races}}, deadlocks, and oversubscription. MPI code breaks from {{c2::mismatched tags}} or ranks and from many small messages. Warp code slows down from {{c3::too many host-device copies}} and problems too small to pay for them.
extra: Non-contiguous data is another Warp pitfall on the table.
